steps.text: Turmeric paper is yellow. Let's find out which substances it can actually detect.
Pick a base first — tap “Soap” (or baking soda).
Now tap “Drop” to drop it onto the turmeric.
The yellow turmeric turns RED/BROWN — turmeric changes colour for BASES.
Now pick an acid — tap “Lemon” — and tap “Drop” again.
It stays YELLOW. Turmeric can't tell acids from neutral substances, so it's a partial indicator — it only detects bases.

coach.mission: Find out what turmeric can detect.
whenStuck: Pick a solution, then tap “Drop” to drop it on the turmeric.
Turmeric reacts to only one kind of solution — try a base.
whenWrong: Turmeric turns red/brown for BASES but stays yellow for acids — it can't detect acids.
Stayed yellow? That solution isn't a base.
whenCorrect: Turmeric is a partial indicator: bases only. Good.
coach.done: You've learned turmeric only detects bases. Explore the others, or move on.
